record.paper_title: Causal Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning: Review and Open Problems
record.original_question: How can generalized off-policy or offline MARL learn from existing observational datasets when the data were collected under unknown mixed policies, multiple hidden decision-making agents influence the environment, and causal assumptions and uncertainties must be modeled to bound uncertainty in the learning process?

evidence.quote: The primary challenge with ofﬂine RL is that we are limited to observational data. Viewed from another angle, this problem comes down to learning structure from data collected under mixed policies and is subject to distribution shift (see Section 2). Explicitly modelling the assumptions and uncertainties can aid in bounding the uncertainties in the learning process (Rosenbaum and Rubin, 1983; MacLehose et al., 2005).

The distribution shift problem is especially exacerbated in the multi-agent problem, where multiple agents with hidden decision policies are inﬂuencing the response of the environment (Yang et al., 2021; Levine et al., 2020; Papoudakis et al., 2019).

This differs from conventional off-policy learning because we lack knowledge of how data was collected. MARL extends the difﬁculty of this generalised setting by involving more decision agents. We believe this is an interesting research direction.

artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research direction in causal multi-agent reinforcement learning. As of 2026, offline MARL with unknown mixed behavior policies and unobserved confounding agents remains an active area: there are partial results (e.g., causal offline RL with sensitivity analysis in single-agent settings, and confounded offline contextual bandits), but no general procedure with sharp identification and finite-sample regret guarantees for the multi-agent confounded setting has been established.
